newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end higher on late buying.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end higher on late buying.

text.p: Singapore shares ended higher on late buying of bluechips before the close on Monday.
"Prices started firming up just after 4.00 when London (fund managers) came in," said a dealer with a local brokerage.
Buying was in selected blue chips and banks stocks but volume was quite light.

"Sentiment is a bit firmer but I think volume is going to remain light because most fund managers are already on holiday," said another dealer. The Straits Times Industrial index ended 4.12 points up at 2,183.26. Volume was a light 70.16 million units with 137 gainers against 173 losers.
Leading the gainers were City Developments and OCBC foreign, both rising 60 cents each to S$12.80 and S$17.30 respectively.

Soft drinks group Fraser & Neave was among the top losers ending at S$14.50, down 40 cents. Dealers said many stock broking firms including DBS Securities had downgraded the company on prospects of a sharp fall in property earnings for the current year.
Financial services group International Factors ended down 25 cents at S$1.20 after major shareholder ECICS said it was not considering any offer for its stake at present.
